text: Why does a public class named Hello have to live in Hello.java?
choices: It does not; the rule is only a convention
Because javac cannot read two classes at once
So the compiler and JVM can find a class by name without searching every file
Because the file system requires it
explanation: It is a convention with teeth — get it wrong and javac refuses. The point is locatability: given a class name, the tooling knows exactly which file to open.
